skill.name: secret-scanner
skill.description: Detect accidentally committed secrets, credentials, and sensitive information in repositories and configuration files.
skill.summary: Find leaked credentials and plan safe remediation before release.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder secrets, and documented scanner commands in SKILL.md. The main real risks are semantic: example reports display raw secret values, and live secret checks lack authorization guardrails. The author should add redaction defaults and explicit safe-use boundaries before publication.

remediation.issue: Reports can disclose raw secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Redact secret values by default and show only type, file, line, fingerprint, and a short suffix when needed.

remediation.issue: Active secret validation lacks authorization controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit owner approval before live validation and prefer offline assessment whenever possible.

remediation.issue: Dangerous remediation commands are presented as direct examples.
remediation.suggestion: Label history rewrite and remote SSH commands as manual, high-impact actions that require confirmation.

remediation.issue: Example credentials match real provider formats.
remediation.suggestion: Replace examples with clearly fake placeholders that do not match production secret patterns.

semantic_findings.title: Secret Reports Include Raw Secret Values
semantic_findings.description: The report examples show full secret values under "Secret Found" fields. A scanner should redact values by default to avoid spreading credentials through logs, tickets, or chat transcripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly place credential-like values in report output and environment examples. This is a clear disclosure pattern even if the values are placeholders.

semantic_findings.title: Live Secret Validation Lacks Authorization Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The instructions tell the user to check whether secrets are still active and exposed publicly. They do not require owner authorization or prohibit authenticating with discovered credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The active-secret check is explicit, but the exact validation method is not specified. The risk is strong because live credential testing can become unauthorized access.

content.value_statement: Leaked credentials create urgent security incidents and costly remediation work. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code review repositories for secrets and plan response steps.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common secret types, including API keys, cloud credentials, database URLs, private keys, and tokens.
Provides regex and entropy based detection guidance for repository reviews.
Suggests established tools such as git-secrets, truffleHog, gitleaks, and detect-secrets.
Outlines severity classification, exposure scope, and remediation priorities for discovered secrets.
Provides prevention guidance for gitignore rules, CI scanning, pre-commit hooks, and secret managers.
Helps structure incident response reports for credential leaks.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include a bundled scanner executable.
It needs user authorization before scanning private repositories, history, or environment files.
It should not validate live credentials without explicit owner approval.
Report examples should be redacted before use in shared logs or tickets.

use_cases.title: Pre-release Repository Review
use_cases.description: Scan a project before publishing to find committed keys, passwords, and sensitive configuration files.

use_cases.title: Credential Leak Triage
use_cases.description: Classify exposed secrets, identify affected files, and create an ordered remediation plan.

use_cases.title: CI Secret Scanning Setup
use_cases.description: Add automated secret checks with common tools, baseline files, and repository guardrails.

prompt_templates.title: Scan Current Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the secret-scanner skill to review my staged changes for obvious secrets. Redact any values in the report.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the secret-scanner skill to audit this repository for credentials, tokens, keys, and sensitive config files. Summarize findings by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Leak Remediation
prompt_templates.scenario: Incident response after a suspected leak
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the secret-scanner skill to build a remediation plan for suspected leaked credentials. Include rotation, history cleanup, and owner notifications.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the secret-scanner skill to design a CI and pre-commit secret scanning workflow for this repository. Include tool choices and failure criteria.

output_examples.input: Review this repository for committed secrets and provide a safe summary.
output: Summary: Two high confidence credential exposures were found.
Finding: AWS access key pattern in a configuration file. Value redacted.
Action: Rotate the key, remove it from history, and add prevention controls.

output_examples.input: Create a remediation checklist for a leaked database URL.
output: Revoke or rotate the database password.
Review access logs for suspicious activity.
Move the URL to a managed secret store.
Clean repository history if the value was committed.

output_examples.input: Recommend CI secret scanning controls for a small engineering team.
output: Add pre-commit scanning for staged files.
Run a full history scan on pull requests.
Fail builds on verified high severity findings.
Store baselines and document exception review.

best_practices: Scan only repositories and files that you are authorized to inspect.
Redact secret values in reports, tickets, logs, and chat transcripts.
Rotate exposed credentials before cleaning repository history.
anti_patterns: Do not paste full production secrets into prompts or reports.
Do not test whether leaked credentials work without explicit owner approval.
Do not treat example keys as safe unless they are clearly placeholders.

faq.question: Does this skill run a scanner by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides detection guidance, tool commands, report structure, and remediation steps.

faq.question: Can it scan git history?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains git history scanning with established tools when repository history is available.

faq.question: Should I include environment files?
faq.answer: Only include them when you are authorized. Redact values in any report or shared output.

faq.question: Does it verify if a secret is still active?
faq.answer: It can help plan verification, but live validation needs explicit owner approval and safe handling rules.

faq.question: Which tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references git-secrets, truffleHog, gitleaks, detect-secrets, BFG Repo Cleaner, and git-filter-repo.

faq.question: What should I do after finding a secret?
faq.answer: Rotate the credential, review access logs, remove it from history, and add prevention controls.
